summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA (published 2026-09-19) asks whether Rivian — down over 85% in five years — is finally a buy. The catalyst: management says point-to-point autonomous capability (Tesla-style unsupervised driving) will launch by end of 2026, which could add high-margin software revenue on top of vehicle sales, given Tesla has over a million paying customers at $99/month. The recently launched lower-priced R2 SUV is selling better than expected, with a $45,000 variant still to come, and cash-flow-from-operations to sales has improved to -31.4% (from below -125% in 2024). Management targets positive gross margin by Q4 2026. He discloses a personal rooting interest — he owns Rivian indirectly via Amazon — but notes he has warned investors away from the stock for years, never having rated it a buy, which proved the right call. Today valuation is the cheapest in years on forward price-to-sales (1.8x). His updated DCF values the company at ~$13/share versus $15.54 market price — still slightly overvalued, but close enough that a ~10% pullback would let him upgrade to a buy. Call: RIVN CONDITIONAL_BUY @ $15.54 market price, DCF value ~$13; would buy after ~10% pullback.
